title: Launch Aftercare Manifest — Stability Garden (Draft)
content:
Purpose:
This note is a practical 'aftercare manifest' for launches: an operational checklist + lightweight calendar + release-notes draft focused on post-deploy stability (the "Stability Garden"). Idea: treat the first 72 hours like a garden bed — plant the release, tend for signs of stress, and prune early anomalies before they spread.

Audience:
- Launch conductor / release lead (owner)
- On-call SRE and release shifters
- Service owners and product PMs for the release

Quick summary:
- Release: backend service v2.3.0 (routing + batching perf changes)
- Launch window: 2026-08-10 02:00 UTC — progressive traffic ramp over 6 hours
- Primary goals: preserve 99th latency SLO, avoid token-cost regression, validate KV cache behavior at scale

Release lead: Ava Chen (owner)
SRE lead: Diego Martinez
PM: Priya Kapoor
Primary Slack channel: #launch-aurora (pin timeline + telemetry links)

Preflight (48–0 hours) — quick checklist (items to confirm in the 48h before window):
- [ ] Final canary perf baseline run completed (load profile: 60k req/min, 95th token length = 180) — GH PR #1984 artifacts attached
- [ ] Telemetry knobs set: sample rate at x100 for request traces, token-level sampling for top 1% by latency
- [ ] Circuit breakers and throttles configured with conservative soft-limits (see ENG-3421)
- [ ] Rollout plan uploaded to Confluence + calendar invite created for 72h watch shifts
- [ ] Pager rotations confirmed for nights 0–3 and weekend (2x coverage daytime, 1x night)
- [ ] Emergency rollback artifact prepared (container tag + migration rollback script) and smoke-test pass

Launch hour play (hour -2 .. +6) — the garden planting window:
- H-120 to H-2: Final canary warmup (10% traffic to canary), verify traces and KV cache hit-rate
- H-2: Night shift handover: read the 'preflight pass' checklist aloud in Slack. Confirm runbooks aligned and ops contacts present
- T0 (02:00 UTC): Begin progressive traffic ramp: 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 75% -> 100% (30m ticks by default; can be paused)
- During ramp: operator tasks every tick:
  - Checkpoint A: 5m after step — 95th latency delta vs baseline, error rate, remote model fallback events
  - Checkpoint B: 15m after step — cost-per-token sampling, top 10 callers list, KV cache miss curve
- Abort/hold criteria (immediate):
  - 95th latency increase > 30% sustained for 10m OR
  - Error rate > 0.5% (user-facing errors) OR
  - Significant model fallback (> 2% of requests)
- If criteria hit: stop ramp, roll back to previous stable percentage for 30m while SRE investigates

Tending the Stability Garden (post-launch days 0–7) — daily cadence and tasks:
Day 0 (first 24h):
- Primary focus: rapid detection and containment
- [ ] Hourly digest in #launch-aurora with: latency charts, error waterfall, top errors (with examples), top vector of callers
- [ ] Verify autoscaler behaviour under sustained requests; ensure no oscillation loops
- [ ] Run spot-check prompts to validate quality (3 curated prompts + 5 random prod prompts)

Day 1–3:
- Focus: signal enrichment and triage
- [ ] Turn on targeted debug traces for any slow endpoints (temporary, scoped to 10% sampling)
- [ ] Evaluate prefix/KV cache warmup curves for typical longest sessions
- [ ] Nightly handoff notes: each shifter posts a short log in the Confluence watch page (template link)

Day 4–7:
- Focus: stabilization and housekeeping
- [ ] Reduce debug sampling to baseline levels; keep some additional sampling for first full-week rolling window
- [ ] Reconcile cost telemetry vs forecast; flag if >10% deviation
- [ ] Prepare 'rollback vs mitigation' decision memo if recurring regressions persist

Stability thresholds (garden rules):
- Latency: 95th should not exceed baseline by more than 15% for >30m; 30% is an immediate hold
- Error budget: immediate remediation if errors cross 0.5%; incremental alerts at 0.1% and 0.25%
- Model fallbacks: investigate if >0.5% in any 15m window; immediate hold if >2%
- Cost: flag if per-token cost deviates >10% from forecast for 1h window

Rollback decision matrix (quick reference):
- Cat A (Immediate rollback): catastrophic user errors (data loss, auth failures), sustained SLA breach >30%
- Cat B (Conditional rollback): perf regressions degrading user experience (latency > 30% and persistent for 30m)
- Cat C (Mitigate in place): non-user-facing internal errors, small quality regressions — apply targeted mitigations, monitor 24–72h

Communications map:
- Who to page: SRE on-call -> release lead -> engineering manager
- Communication channels: #launch-aurora (ops chatter), #status (customer-facing), incident bridge (Zoom link pinned)
- Template: short subject lines, link to digest + key graphs, and explicit ask (rollback / mitigation / triage)

Release notes (draft) — to be edited for external release notes and internal digest:
- Headline: Service routing and batching improvements (v2.3.0) — reduced average per-token CPU by ~12% in canary; rolling deployment Aug 10 2026
- Notable changes:
  - Introduced adaptive batching logic to improve throughput for mixed-length queries
  - Tighter default KV cache expiry and improved cache warmup heuristics
  - Routing policy change: prefer low-latency host pools for latency-sensitive routes (opt-in via config)
- Migration notes for integrators:
  - No schema changes; clients may see different cold-start latencies for long sessions while cache warms
  - If you pin to model variants, confirm compatibility with new routing policy (docs link)
- Known issues (recorded):
  - Intermittent increased miss-rate on prefix cache in certain regional traffic patterns (investigating)
  - Rare 502s observed in canary under pathological streaming cancellations — mitigation steps in runbook

Observability and telemetry (practical knobs):
- Dashboards to watch (links to dashboards should be pinned to Slack):
  - Latency by route (95/99), Error waterfall, Cache hit-rate by host pool, Token cost breakdown by caller
- Quick trace recipe: when investigating high-p95, collect 20 traces across caller segments and token-length buckets (short, mid, long)
- Sampling recommendations for first 72 hours: trace x100, token-sample top 1% by latency, request-sample 1:50 baseline after day 2

Experiment & rollouts notes (A/B):
- Canary config: 10% opaque cohort for 3h, then progressive ramp if no regressions
- Split-testing: keep 10% of traffic for variant B (legacy routing) if we want a side-by-side comparison for 48h
- Metric to decide final flip: p95 latency + top-10 customer error delta + cost-per-token delta (scorecard to be produced)

Field notes / TODOs (notes to self, informal):
- Add a lightweight watchlist script that publishes hourly digest automatically (shard into small CSV with top 10 err messages).
- Confirm the Confluence watch template is writable by night shifters (permission hiccup last time).
- Check whether the client libraries will accept the new routing header by default or require minor bump.
- Unresolved: should we widen the KV cache TTL for sessions > 1k tokens? Needs product input.

After-action sketch (placeholder):
- Post-launch, collect: 72h incident timeline, latency/cost delta table, churned callers list, customer-impact summary.
- Suggested owners for the AAR: release lead (Ava) for coordination, SRE (Diego) for telemetry, PM (Priya) for customer comms.

Appendix:
- Quick links: Confluence page (linked_artifacts), GH PR #1984 (linked_artifacts), Jira ENG-3421 (linked_artifacts)
- Short list of shift templates and digest sample (paste into the Confluence watch page):
  - HOURLY DIGEST TEMPLATE: 1-sentence summary; 3 bullet signals (latency/error/cost); top error examples; immediate actions; link to graphs

Signature: Ava Chen — release lead (draft).
